header: The Kolkata price of petrol, diesel and LPG over the last year (the chart under the fuel card). PETROL AND DIESEL come from the Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell (PPAC) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas: its retail-selling-price table of the four metros is an official record with one row for every day since 16 June 2017 (a PDF, "Table Posted" each morning). Read with pdf-parse, each row is "12-Nov-26102.12 111.21 107.77 113.51 12-Nov-2695.20 97.83 99.55 99.82": the date and the petrol prices of Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata, then the date and the diesel prices of the same four. Kolkata is the fourth of each. LPG (domestic 14.2 kg) has no PPAC table. The only free record found is GoodReturns' monthly table for Kolkata ("Last 10 Months LPG Rate in Kolkata"), so the LPG chart is monthly and shorter (ten months and today). No source read has Kolkata's LPG price for November or December 2025, and I guess none. My self-check makes a changed page a loud error and never a wrong number: every row must have the same date on both sides, every day of the year must be there, every price must be plausible, the table must be fresh, and each LPG month's stated change must equal the difference between its price and the month before. A failure throws, and the route falls back to the copy kept with the app (marked as such).

members.name: date
doc: Format YYYY-MM-DD: for a month its first day, for today's LPG price today.

members.name: grain
doc: One point for every day, or one for every month.

members.name: savedOn
doc: Set when the series is the copy kept with the app, saved on this date, because the live source did not answer.

members.name: notes
doc: What could not be had, and what came from the saved copy, in words for the card.

symbols.name: ROW
doc: "12-Nov-26102.12 111.21 107.77 113.51 12-Nov-2695.20 97.83 99.55 99.82": pdf-parse glues a date to the price after it and the layout reader does not, so I read both.

symbols.name: ppacPdfLink
doc: The address of the PDF on PPAC's own page. Its name carries the date and a number that changes every day, so I find it on the page, and I follow only a PPAC address.

symbols.name: parsePpacKolkata
symbols.sig: export function parsePpacKolkata(text: string, now: DateTime = DateTime.now().setZone(ZONE)): PpacKolkata
doc: I return Kolkata's petrol and diesel price for every day from the same date one year before today to the latest day of the table (both ends in; the route carries the last price on to today). `now` fixes today for the tests.

symbols.name: parseLpgKolkata
symbols.sig: export function parseLpgKolkata(text: string, now: DateTime = DateTime.now().setZone(ZONE)): FuelPoint[]
doc: Kolkata's domestic 14.2 kg LPG price for each month of GoodReturns' table, with today's price as the last point.

symbols.name: Snapshot
doc: I keep only the days on which a price CHANGED (petrol, diesel), and the LPG points as they are.

members.name: through
doc: The last day covered by the petrol and diesel record.

symbols.name: toChanges
symbols.sig: export function toChanges(points: FuelPoint[]): Array<[string, number]>
doc: Returns the days on which the value changed (the first day always counts).

symbols.name: expandChanges
symbols.sig: export function expandChanges(changes: Array<[string, number]>, through: string): FuelPoint[]
doc: Gives every day from the first change to `through`, each holding the price of the last change.

symbols.name: seriesFromSnapshot
symbols.sig: export function seriesFromSnapshot(s: Snapshot, id: FuelId): FuelSeries

symbols.name: inYearWindow
symbols.sig: export function inYearWindow(s: FuelSeries, now: DateTime = DateTime.now()): { series: FuelSeries; carriedFrom: string | null }
doc: The one-year window of a daily series (petrol, diesel): from the same date one year before today (the price in force on that day) to TODAY. I carry the last published price on to today because a fuel price stays until the day it is changed. Returns the series and the day the carrying began (null when the record already ends today). I leave a monthly series (LPG) as it is: its source holds only ten months.

symbols.name: validSeries
symbols.sig: export function validSeries(s: FuelSeries | null): s is FuelSeries
doc: I treat a series as usable when it has points in date order, with plausible values.

behaviours: the PDF is found on PPAC's page by its name (which carries a date and a number that change daily)
a relative link on the page is made whole; an address on another host, or not https, is refused; a page without the link is an error

a year of days from the same date a year before today (13 Nov 2025; today is 13 Nov 2026) to the latest day of the table (12 Nov 2026), both ends in, is 365 days, petrol and diesel alike, each day once and in order
Kolkata is the fourth price of each table: petrol 105.41 a year ago and 113.51 now, diesel 92.02 and 99.82 (not Delhi's 102.12 or 95.20)
the days on which Kolkata petrol changed: 1 Jan 105.45, then 15, 19, 23 and 25 May 2026 up to 113.51; diesel on the four May days
the highest petrol price of the year is 113.51 and the lowest 105.41; diesel 99.82 and 92.02
the text of a layout reader (spaces between the date and the price) is read the same
the page can be asked a few days late (the table is posted each morning) but not a week late: 19 Nov is fine, 25 Nov is out of date
a missing day, a row whose two dates differ, a price that is not plausible, and a table that is not there are each an error, never a number
ten months and today: Jan 2026 879, Feb 879, Mar 939 (the rise of 60), Apr, May 939, Jun 968 (the rise of 29) to Oct, and today 968 on 13 Nov 2026
when the table already has the current month, today's price replaces it (no month twice)
each month's stated change must equal its price less the month before: a column read in the wrong place is an error
a missing month, an implausible price, and a page without the table are each an error
the saved copy says when it was saved and through which day
the saved copy of petrol and diesel, expanded to every day, is exactly what PPAC's table gives for the same window (from 13 Nov 2025)
the saved copy of LPG is exactly what the table gives
all three saved series are usable; a series that is empty, out of order or implausible is not
changes and days go round: only the days of a change are kept, and each day holds the last price
the route reads nothing of the caller (GET takes no request) and its two sources are fixed addresses
the two kinds are asked separately (a failure of one does not take the other down), each falls back to the saved copy, and all three missing is an error
pdf-parse is read from its lib file, kept external and included in the deployed route (or the PDF engine would be missing on the host)
petrol is carried on to today: the table ends on 12 Nov 2026, so the chart ends on 13 Nov 2026 with that day's price (a fuel price stays until it is changed), and says from which day it was carried
a record that already ends today is not carried
the saved copy is cut at the same date a year back (13 Nov 2025) and carried to today, whatever its own first day
LPG (monthly, ten months at the source) is left as it is: the source cannot give a year
